title: Sales Enablement Playbook: Positioning, Pricing, Case Studies & Security FAQ
author: Aisha Raman
content:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook centralizes Redwood Inference's core external-facing sales materials for field use: short-form positioning and messaging, competitive brief, recommended pitch deck flow, pricing guidance with example TCOs, two lean case studies, and a prospect-facing security FAQ. Use this as the canonical source for slide decks, one-pagers, and discovery call scripts.

Audience: AEs, SEs, solution architects, growth reps, and marketing who need consistent, engineering-forward messaging.

Executive summary

- Core positioning: Redwood Inference is a developer-first inference platform that makes production LLM serving predictable, economical, and secure across Hosted (Redwood API), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools), and Private (VPC / on-prem) deployment modes.
- Primary value props: predictable latency & throughput, measurable cost controls, unified operational tooling, and enterprise controls for compliance-sensitive customers.
- Primary personas: platform engineers, ML engineers, product engineering leads, and cloud architecture / security stakeholders.

Positioning & messaging (talk tracks)

Elevator pitch (15s): "Redwood Inference gives engineering teams a single runtime and control plane to run high-throughput, low-latency LLM inference across hosted, reserved, and private deployments—so you get predictable performance and lower per-token costs without building an ops stack."

3 core messages (for discovery calls)

1) Production-first economics: "We reduce your per-token cost with intelligent batching, prefix/KV caching, and model routing while preserving latency SLOs—typically 2–4x cost savings over unoptimized single-instance serving for real-world workloads."
2) Unified operations: "Same API, same dashboards, same rollout controls across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private—no rework when you move from PoC to production or from cloud to private networks."
3) Enterprise controls and resilience: "SLA-backed Dedicated capacity, private control planes, KMS integrations, and fallback routing for graceful degradation during capacity events."

Message accents by persona

- ML Engineer: focus on model versioning, quantization profiles, and eval integration for regression alerts.
- Platform/Infra: emphasize autoscaling policies, GPU utilization dashboards, and reserved capacity pricing.
- Security/Compliance: highlight VPC Private deploys, KMS/HSM support, audit logs, and SOC/ISO evidence.

Competitive brief (one-page summary)

Top competitors: Managed LLM APIs (Competitor A, Competitor B), Cloud provider endpoints (Cloud X Managed Endpoints), and self-hosted inference runtimes (OpenSourceRuntime Y or Vendor Z).

Differentiation matrix (key attributes)

- Performance predictability: Redwood — High (dedicated pools + routing) | Competitor A — Medium | Cloud X — Medium
- Cost controls: Redwood — High (batching, caching, quantization guidance) | Competitors — Low/Medium
- Deployment flexibility (Hosted/Dedicated/Private): Redwood — Full | Cloud X — Hosted/Dedicated only | Self-hosted — Private only (requires ops)
- Enterprise controls & compliance: Redwood — Strong (KMS, audit logs, private control plane) | Competitor B — Varies

Competitive positioning bullets for calls

- To customers comparing to managed API provider: "If you need simple PoC speed, managed APIs are fine; choose Redwood when you care about unit economics and predictable latency in production."
- To customers comparing to cloud endpoints: "Cloud endpoints scale but can be expensive at token volumes and don’t give a single operational model across private and hosted environments."
- To customers considering self-hosted runtimes: "Self-hosting delivers control but is expensive to operate and lacks a unified control plane and observability out-of-the-box. Redwood balances control with operational ease."

Suggested competitive rebuttals (short)

- "We’re already on Cloud X": "We integrate with common cloud infra and can sit alongside Cloud X for migration/bursting while reducing per-token costs for inference-heavy routes."
- "Open-source runtime is free": "Open-source lowers license costs but moves the operational burden to your team; Redwood removes that burden and adds optimizations (kernel selection, continuous batching) you would otherwise need to engineer."

Pitch deck recommended flow (10–12 slides)

1) Title + one-line customer pain: "LLM features are expensive and brittle at scale."
2) Market & opportunity (why inference matters now).
3) Customer pain / typical architecture (model hosting + ad-hoc infra).
4) Redwood solution overview (Hosted, Dedicated, Private).
5) How it works (runtime, smart routing, caching, deployment abstraction).
6) Performance and economics (benchmarks: 95th-latency <150ms for common chat workloads; 2–4x unit-cost reduction vs naive serving).
7) Security & compliance (VPC, KMS, audit logs, SOC/ISO artifacts).
8) Case studies (short metrics).
9) Pricing & commercial options (self-serve, reserved capacity, enterprise licensing).
10) Deployment options & proof plan (POC steps and success criteria).
11) Next steps / ask (trial, pilot, stakeholder workshop).

Slide assets to include (repo references)

- Latency & throughput benchmark charts (links: /assets/benchmarks/2026-q3).
- Cost comparison tables by workload (chat vs embeddings vs rerank).
- Architecture diagrams for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private.

Pricing guidance (field-facing)

Pricing models (high level)

- Hosted (Redwood API): usage-based (per-token generation / per-embedding unit) with free-tier credits for self-serve evaluation.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): monthly/annual commit for GPU pools; priced by committed GPU-hours with predictable throughput and SLA credits.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): platform fee + optional support tier and deployment services (one-time onboarding fee + annual maintenance).

Rule-of-thumb pricing examples (helpful for early discovery)

- Small PoC (hosted): < $2k/month with hourly throttling and 10k generated tokens/day assumptions.
- Mid-market product team (dedicated): dedicated 4xA100-equivalent pool with predictable throughput ~ $25k–$60k/month depending on burst capacity and retention policies.
- Enterprise private deployment: platform license $150k+/yr + deployment services; typical three-year TCO depends on on-prem infra.

How to build a TCO for customers (short checklist)

1) Collect token volumes & request size distributions (chat vs embeddings).
2) Identify latency SLOs and peak concurrency.
3) Model baseline cost (current vendor or self-hosted).
4) Estimate Redwood cost (hosted per-token or dedicated commit) + expected batching/cache efficiency improvements.
5) Show savings scenarios (conservative, expected, aggressive).

Commercial packaging guidance (objections and playbook)

- If customer is price-sensitive: start with hosted trial + quantifiable TCO comparison; schedule cost-optimization review after 30-day usage to recommend batching/quantization.
- If customer requires compliance: move directly to Private evaluation; provide SOC/ISO evidence pack and KMS/HSM integration options.

Case studies (two concise vignettes)

1) EdTech platform (Growth-to-Prod):
- Customer: anonymized-edtech (Series B)
- Challenge: high variance in response latency for chat tutors and rising token costs as usage scaled.
- Solution: Moved from single-instance self-hosted model to Redwood Dedicated with KV caching for common prefixes and routing to quantized model variants for low-risk traffic.
- Outcome: 3.2x reduction in per-token inference cost, 40% reduction in 95th percentile latency (from 220ms -> 132ms), and a predictable monthly bill enabling finance to approve a 12-month commit.

2) Regulated financial SaaS (Compliance & Data Residency):
- Customer: enterprise-fin-saas (Fortune 500)
- Challenge: must keep PII in-country and meet audit controls; previous vendors lacked private control plane and KMS integration.
- Solution: Private deployment (VPC) + KMS integration, dedicated capacity for peak trading-window inference, audit-log ingestion into customer SIEM.
- Outcome: Passed internal security review, achieved SOC evidence consumption for auditors, and reduced mean time to detect inference anomalies via Redwood Console dashboards (MTTA improved from days to hours).

Security FAQ (prospect-facing, short answers)

Q: Where will my data live?
A: For Hosted customers, data lives in region you select and is logically isolated per-tenant. For Private customers, data never leaves your VPC/on-prem environment unless you configure exports.

Q: Do you support customer KMS/HSM?
A: Yes. We support common KMS integrations (AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS, Azure Key Vault) and HSM-backed key material for Private deployments.

Q: What logging and audit capabilities are available?
A: Audit logs include request/response metadata (no raw PII unless enabled), key rotation events, deployment changes, and admin actions. Logs can be streamed to your SIEM or S3.

Q: How do you handle model updates and potential regressions?
A: Redwood provides model versioning, canary rollouts, and quality monitoring tied to eval prompt sets. If regressions are detected, automatic rollback policies can be configured.

Q: Is customer data used to train models?
A: By default, Redwood does not use customer request data to train public models. Data-use policies are clearly defined in contracts; private deployments give you full control over training/extraction.

Q: What compliance evidence do you provide?
A: SOC/ISO summaries, penetration-test reports, and onboarding checklists are available. For enterprise customers we provide tailored evidence packs during security review.

Sales objection handling (short scripts)

- "We already have infra / self-hosted runtime": "Great — many large customers use Redwood alongside self-hosted stacks. We focus on operationalizing inference: plug Redwood into your pipeline for critical routes while keeping other models self-hosted. That cuts ops burden and frees teams to ship features."
- "Your pricing is higher than open-source": "Open-source shifts long-term maintenance and optimization work to internal teams; Redwood accelerates time-to-value and delivers optimizations (batching, kernel selection) that reduce your total cost of ownership. We can run a 30-day pilot to quantify impact."

Discovery -> Pilot -> Close playbook (recommended steps)

1) Initial discovery (30–45 min): gather persona list, performance targets, estimated token volumes, and compliance constraints.
2) Data & infra review: confirm region, network options (VPC peering, transit), and KMS requirements.
3) Pilot setup (2–4 weeks): hosted trial or dedicated POC; define success criteria (latency, throughput, cost improvements).
4) Evaluation & optimization (2–6 weeks): implement batching, cache hints, and quantized model variants; run evals to validate quality.
5) Commercial proposal & onboarding: present recommended package (hosted credits vs dedicated commit vs private license) and rollout plan.
